items.title: Alibaba Seata Resolves Idempotence, Dangling, and Empty Rollback Issues in TCC Mode

claimMappingReview: Seata user guide covers business-implemented checking/reservation and mutually exclusive Confirm or Cancel; no claim that every TCC action is run sequentially or arbitrary RPCs gain database rollback.

Fence old actual-reading record supports durable Try reservation, control state/business-resource local atomicity, repeated-request effect protection and empty rollback/dangling boundaries. The old example remains explicitly 2022/Seata1.5.1/reference-only, not a claim all TCC implementations solve failures automatically.

Inventory teaching states conserve four units and original independent success/cancel branches remain unchanged. Repeated confirmation/release must not consume/release twice or switch a persisted outcome.

The entire old article/research and AWS retry/developer-doc footnotes remain. Selected core list omits a duplicate-title developer guide and AWS whose personal byline was not established, without inventing an author or claiming old citations disappeared.

Three pinned Apache repository files were separately retrieved26th for exact titles and explicit Fence author Zhu Jinjun; locally verified full file bytes/SHA/frontmatter lines and existing independent review-record Git identities. No new technical reread or canonical GET is claimed.

claimMappingReview: Transactions is explicitly the same local transaction controlling transactional data; same database/machine/service count does not establish a joint commit. PG18 versioned canonical is supported by retained navigation identifying PostgreSQL18; original moving current links remain in old text.
XA Transactions covers supported coordinated resource branches, without identical-millisecond visibility, universal global isolation or treating RPCs in a code block as a resource protocol.
Retry pattern covers lost replies/possible effects and conditional bounded retry; permanent business refusal is not fixed by indefinite retries.

Compensating Transaction pattern supports business-dependent compensation, visible intermediate state, durable recoverable progress and potential manual handling, not overwriting an old snapshot or unconditional eventual success.

Idempotent Consumer pattern independently supports atomically committing a stable processed-operation key with effects and protecting concurrent duplicates; retaining it avoids misattributing this stronger rule to the Retry wrapper. Applies beyond messaging, so the synchronous example is not relabeled a queue protocol.

Five selected references preserve all old AWS/Saga/outbox/Seata footnotes and original research. Old blocked AWS navigation reread remains disclosed; no newly successful AWS reread or guessed personal author is invented.

claimMappingReview: MySQL XA Transactions supports resource/transaction-manager coordination and prepare then common outcome; XA is an interface layer, not a parallel algorithm to2PC or a wrapper making ordinary RPCs transactional.

XA Transaction States and PREPARE TRANSACTION support durable prepared state without commit, recoverability and held locks/resource cost; disconnect or a local timeout does not automatically resolve the prepared transaction. No manual production force-resolution advice is introduced.

Narayana is retained as the explicit old-read basis for logging the stable common decision before final instructions and recovering the prior decision. The old Chinese project-document label is not passed off as an original title. New pinned title/index/pom/migration metadata establishes the exact book identity without claiming a fresh technical chapter reread.

Unanimous ready responses, prepared rejection before a commit decision, and prepared-but-unknown waiting/recovery remain different branches. Participants apply one stable result at different times; no identical-millisecond visibility, universal global snapshot or arbitrary new choice on restart.

All original article five footnotes including Oracle cross-check, original PostgreSQL Two-Phase Transactions research, navigation semantics and prior independent editorial24Oct read evidence remain retained. No performance/market-share or unrecorded product-version claims.
